- public datasheets;
- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
- **Records in a clean folder.** Each record on the `records` branch also
  keeps the harness's own test results and the hashes of their outputs.
  Records before SR-1-SR-2 also keep the spec experiments' outputs (memory
  dumps, captures, audio); since then a record keeps only their names and
  SHA-256 (`spec-experiments.sha256`), and older records stay as they are.
  Clean sessions never fetch the records branch wholesale (no `git archive`, checkout or
  lazy fetch of a whole record or of the branch): they fetch only named
  files of the firmware's own records, `report.json`, `report.md` and
  named logs under `logs/`, one path at a time. `tools/clean-update.sh`
  also stops if a file under a `harness/` or `spec-experiments/` folder,
  or under the excluded folders, is in `.git` through any branch, the
  records branch included (since M1, after a wholesale fetch brought 17
  such outputs into a clean folder; docs/EXPOSURE.md).
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).

## Pull requests and merging

- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
  links to the CI run and the record).
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main, and the similarity
  audit's report beside it (`records/<sha>/audit/`) only by
  `.github/workflows/audit.yml`'s record job (docs/AUDIT.md). Both use the

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

content.content:
<!--
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
-->

# The similarity audit

This repository says its firmware was written clean-room, without the FM-1's
GPL community firmwares (CONTRIBUTING.md). The audit backs that up with a
measurement. On every push to main, a CI job compares our firmware with
every FM-1 firmware repository it can find, and with an unrelated control
project, and puts the scores in the commit's record. Requirements:
R-AUDIT-1 to R-AUDIT-6 (docs/REQUIREMENTS.md).

Nobody working on this repository reads the targets. The spec side found
them from repository metadata alone. The job fetches them only inside CI,
and its logs and outputs hold scores and file names, never code. When the
job flags a pair, only an **auditor** may look (below).

## What is compared

- **Ours:** the C files under `firmware/` (`.c`, `.h`, and C++ suffixes if
  we ever have any). Assembly (`.S`) and linker scripts (`.ld`) are not
  compared: JPlag's C front end doesn't read them. `vendor/` is not ours
  and is never compared.
- **Base code:** the vendored JieLi SDK headers
  (`vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib`). JPlag drops matches with base code, so
  code that both sides took from the SDK doesn't count against us.
- **Targets:** the C and C++ files of every target (below), at its pinned
  commit. `audit/targets.json` lists the targets; `paths` limits a target
  to some of its folders.
- **The control:** the C files of `raspberrypi/pico-examples` at tag
  `sdk-2.2.0`, commit `4c3a3dc0196dd426fddd709616d0da984e027bab`
  (BSD-3-Clause; `audit/audit.json`).

## The targets, from metadata only

`tools/audit-discover.py` builds `audit/targets.json` from
`audit/discover.json`. It asks GitHub's REST API, and `git ls-remote`, for
repository names, owners, descriptions, licences, languages, fork lists and
commit and tree SHAs. It never opens a target's files, README or web pages,
and never prints a description. A target is:

- **a seed:** Felucca (`hugelton/Felucca`), dinghy (`zvenson/dinghy`), the
  `fm1-sid/` and `probes/` folders of fm1-emu
  (`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu`), M-VAVE's `m-vave/fm1_open`, and the other
  FM-1 repositories of Felucca's author (`felucca-bsp`,
  `Felucca-Engines`, `Felucca-WebApp`, `felucca-mirror`);
- **a search hit:** a repository that one of the search queries finds and
  whose description names the FM-1, Felucca, GHOULBOX or Hortator. A
  repository that only matches by name must also be written in C or C++.
  "M-VAVE" or "dinghy" alone don't count, because they also name other
  products, boats and tools. dinghy's own lineage is found through its
  fork tree, and through descriptions that name the FM-1;
- **any fork of a target, to any depth.** A fork inherits its parent's
  `paths` and licence override.

**As found on 2026-10-22:** 780 repositories, after two passes whose
search results differed a little. Of these, 516 are scored and 262 are
duplicates by tree. The other 2 are empty. Of the 516 scored, 381 are classed `gpl`, 47
`permissive`, 43 `other` and 45 `none`.

The owner chose this wide net on 2026-10-22: every FM-1 repository, not
only Felucca's and dinghy's lineage. A target that turns out to be
unrelated costs only CI minutes. A target that is missed weakens the
claim.

Each target is **pinned** at its default branch's head commit, together
with that commit's tree. The job checks both. Targets whose tree (and
`paths`) is already in the list are marked `duplicate` and not fetched
again. Seeds come first, then other repositories, then forks, so a fork
that changed nothing is covered by the repository it copies. Empty
repositories are listed as `empty`.

Each target's **licence** is classed from its metadata as `gpl` (GPL,
LGPL, AGPL), `permissive` (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, WTFPL, CC0 and
similar), `other` (MPL-2.0, NOASSERTION, anything else) or `none` (no
licence). fm1-emu's metadata says MIT, but `fm1-sid/` is a GPL firmware
(docs/EXPOSURE.md), so that seed is classed `gpl`. The report shows each
target's class beside its scores. A flagged pair fails the job whatever
the licence.

**Unresolved:** *Felucca Salt* and *Felucca 8 Patterns*, both named in
CONTRIBUTING.md's forbidden list. No repository for either was found from
metadata on 2026-10-22; they may be distributed only as binaries. They are
listed in `discover.json` and in every report, and the owner adds a URL if
one turns up.

**Limits:** only the default branch is pinned; work on other branches,
and code in git submodules, is not fetched. A repository that neither
search finds nor any target's fork tree reaches is missed. Repositories
deleted after pinning are reported as `not fetched`.

### Rediscovery

`.github/workflows/audit-discover.yml` runs on the first day of every month,
and on demand. It runs `tools/audit-discover.py --write`, which uses
metadata only, as above. If any target is new, gone or has moved to a new
commit, it opens an issue titled "audit: the targets have changed" that
lists those repositories by name, or updates that issue if one is still
open. The rewritten `audit/targets.json` is kept as the run's `targets`
artifact for 90 days. The job has read access to the code and write
access to issues only: it cannot push a branch or open a pull request. It
never fetches a target's code: only the audit job does that.

Search results vary from run to run, so a target already in
`targets.json` stays even when this month's searches miss it. It is
dropped only when `git ls-remote` can no longer reach its repository. A
run also reuses the stored tree of every target whose head hasn't moved, so
only new or moved repositories cost an API request for their tree. When
GitHub's rate limit runs out, it waits for the reset time GitHub gives.
Each run prints how many requests it made.

New repository names can trip the separation check (C-SEP-TERMS), as
`audit/targets.json` already did once: a repository named after another
M-VAVE keyboard that the emulator also models. In principle they could
trip the privacy check (C-PRIVATE) too. A spec-side session reviews such a
hit. A separation hit gets an entry by hash in
`config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`; a privacy hit goes to the owner.

A spec-side session turns the issue into a pull request:
1. Download the newest run's artifact, as the issue says
   (`gh run download <run> -n targets`), and replace `audit/targets.json`
   with it. Don't rerun the discovery locally: search results vary, and the
   artifact is what the issue lists.
2. Do the review just described for any separation or privacy hit.
3. Open the pull request with "Closes #<issue>". Because a person opens it,
   `ci` runs as usual, and the owner merges it with the button.

## The method

JPlag 6.3.0 (the jar with dependencies, checked against its SHA-256 in
`audit/audit.json`) runs in the Java 25 image `eclipse-temurin`, pinned by
digest, with no network. Its settings:
- the C language module, with JPlag's default minimum match of 12 tokens;
- **every file is its own submission**, because JPlag drops a whole
  submission when one of its files fails to parse;
- our files and the control's files are the "new" submissions, and the
  target files are the "old" ones. JPlag compares every new file with every
  old one, and never compares two old ones;
- each target file is scored **once per blob**: forks share most files, and
  a report lists every target and path that holds a flagged blob;
- comparisons with no match at all are not written (`-m 0.000001`), which
  loses no score.

Each file pair gets three numbers:
- the **longest match**: the longest run of tokens the two files share;
- **max**: the matched tokens over the smaller file's tokens;
- **avg**: the matched tokens over the mean of the two files' tokens.

JPlag compares token structure, not names, so renaming identifiers does
not hide a copy.

### Why the longest match, not the ratio

Before choosing, the spec side scored the control against an unrelated
permissive embedded project: TinyUSB's `src/` at commit
`3fa7b06d284c0ac1d1078a0a2d09dceb405499e7` (MIT), 244 control files against
190 TinyUSB files, 27,492 file pairs, with the same settings. Nothing
GPL was involved.

| Score | Median | 99th percentile | 99.9th percentile | Highest |
|-------|--------|-----------------|-------------------|---------|
| Longest match (tokens) | 0 | 13 | 17 | 33 |
| max (ratio) | 0 | 0.116 | 0.325 | 0.857 |

The ratio reaches 0.857 between two unrelated projects: a short file is
easily "mostly matched" by chance. The longest match stays short between
unrelated code, while a copied function gives one long run. So the gate
uses the longest match, and the report shows `max` and `avg` beside it.

### The threshold

The job **fails** when a pair of one of our files and a target file has a
longest match above the **threshold**:

> threshold = the control's longest match with any target it is not
> related to + 24 tokens

The control's highest score is what chance gives, in this run, against
these targets. That covers code idioms, common libraries and headers the
targets share with any embedded C. The margin of 24 tokens is twice
JPlag's minimum match: three or four C statements of identical structure,
beyond the longest run that unrelated embedded code shares with any
target. The calibration's highest chance run was 33 tokens, so the
threshold works out at about 55 to 60 tokens: six to eight lines of the
same code, which chance did not produce once in 27,492 pairs.

**Control-related targets.** A target that the control itself matches by
more than **100 tokens** is not unrelated to it. Some FM-1 repository might
carry Raspberry Pi code, for example a recovery tool for a Pico. Such a
target:
- is listed in the report as *control-related*;
- is left out of the baseline, so it doesn't raise the threshold for every
  other target;
- is judged against the control's own score there: a pair of ours fails
  above that score plus 24.

A file that several targets hold gets the strictest of their thresholds.
C-AUDIT-CONTROL fails if more than 10% of the scored targets are
control-related. The control would then be a poor yardstick for these
targets, and the owner chooses another, by pull request. A dry run showed
why this rule is needed. Against TinyUSB as a whole (not only its `src/`),
the control shares a 107-token run, because TinyUSB's own Raspberry Pi port
overlaps pico-examples' USB examples. One target like that would otherwise
have lifted the threshold for all of them.

### What the gate cannot see

- **Small files.** A pair can fail only if its longest match is above the
  threshold. A verbatim copy of a file shorter than the threshold therefore
  can't fail the job. Today our files are 54, 20 and 16 tokens long, so an
  exact copy of one of them would show as a top pair with `max` 1.0 but
  would not fail the job. The report lists each of our files' token counts,
  and its top pairs with `max`, so a reader can see this. The gate gets
  stronger as the firmware grows.
- **Drift.** The control is fixed and the firmware grows. Larger files have
  more chances to share a run by accident. The control's score, measured
  against the same targets in the same run, is the yardstick. If the
  firmware ever dwarfs the control, a larger control is chosen, by pull
  request.
- **Reordered or rewritten code** splits a copied run into shorter ones.
  Clean-room work is meant to prevent that kind of derivation, and the audit
  is evidence for it, not proof.

### Why this control

`raspberrypi/pico-examples` is:
- permissive (BSD-3-Clause);
- pinned at a release tag;
- embedded C of the same kind as ours: startup and clocks, timers,
  interrupts, UART, GPIO, DMA, audio and display examples;
- mostly small files, as ours are.

It is written for a different chip family (RP2040 and RP2350) and has
nothing to do with the FM-1, so its similarity to the targets is chance
and shared idiom, not copying. Its scores measure the noise floor that ours
are judged against. TinyUSB, used for the calibration above, was not chosen
as the control: an FM-1 firmware could reasonably vendor TinyUSB for USB
MIDI, which would raise the baseline.

## Running it

`.github/workflows/audit.yml`:
- runs on every push to main, and on demand (`workflow_dispatch`, with a
  choice of set);
- never runs for pull requests: there is no such trigger, and both jobs
  also require main.

GitHub offers the on-demand run only once the workflow file is on main, so
its first run is the push that merges it.

- **Sets.** `full` scores every target that isn't a duplicate. `fast`
  scores the four seeds Felucca, dinghy, fm1-emu's `fm1-sid/` (with
  `probes/`) and `fm1_open`. Pushes to main run `full`: the first run
  (below) took under 4 minutes. If a full run ever takes more than about 30
  minutes, push runs switch to `fast` and a nightly schedule runs `full`.
  That is one change to `audit.yml`'s triggers, by pull request, and this
  page then says so.
- **Self-test first.** Each run starts with `tools/audit.py selftest`. It
  builds a made-up local target that holds verbatim copies of our files,
  runs the whole pipeline on it, and checks that each of our files is found
  and that the leak check passes (C-AUDIT-SELFTEST). No GPL code is
  involved. If the self-test fails, the audit still runs and is recorded,
  and the job fails at the end.
- **Job `audit`** has read-only permissions, no environment and no
  secrets. For each target in turn it:
  1. fetches the pinned commit into a temporary folder: depth 1, blob-less,
     with a sparse checkout of the C and C++ files only;
  2. checks the commit's tree against the pin;
  3. copies each file it hasn't seen before into the pool;
  4. deletes the checkout.

  The fetches run eight at a time (`fetch_workers`), but files join the
  pool in the list's order, so the report is the same from run to run.
  Then it runs JPlag once over the whole pool. JPlag's console output goes
  to a log in the temporary folder that is never shown, because a parse
  error quotes source. Its report archive embeds the files it compared, so
  the tool reads only three JSON members of it (comparisons, failed files,
  token counts: names and numbers), then deletes it. The temporary folder
  is removed whatever happens, and the job says so. Nothing is cached. The
  only artifact is `report.json` and `report.md`.
- **The leak check (C-AUDIT-LEAK).** Before the report is written, every
  line of every target file that is 24 characters or longer (after
  trimming) is looked for in it. On a hit the report is cut down to its
  checks, saying the leak check failed.
- **Job `record`** never sees a target. It:
  1. downloads the artifact;
  2. checks that it holds only that report (`tools/audit.py
     check-artifact`);
  3. appends it to the commit's record on the `records` branch, at
     `records/<sha>/audit/<run>-<attempt>/`, with the `records`
     environment's deploy key.

  If the records workflow is pushing at the same moment, it starts again
  from the branch's tip.

### The report

`report.json` and `report.md` hold:
- the pinned JPlag, Java image and control, the control's highest longest
  match with an unrelated target, the threshold and the margin, and the
  control-related targets;
- the checks (C-AUDIT-JPLAG, -PIN, -CONTROL, -SCORE, -LEAK) and their
  traceability to R-AUDIT-*;
- **our top 20 file pairs**: our file, the target repositories and paths
  holding the matched file (the first ten of them, and how many there are),
  each with its licence class, and the longest match, max and avg;
- the control's top five pairs, and its best pair with our own files;
- each of our files' token counts. A file that matched nothing anywhere
  (no run of 12 tokens) shows `no match` with no count: JPlag leaves such a
  file out of its index. It was still parsed and compared; the self-test,
  which fails unless every one of our files is found, shows that it parses;
- every target: its pinned commit, licence class, files fetched (and how
  many were new to the pool), our longest and the control's longest match
  with it, and how many of its files JPlag could not parse or found too
  small;
- the flagged pairs, every place listed; pairs accepted by an auditor's
  finding; how many targets were skipped as duplicates or empty; and the
  unresolved names.

### The first run

The push that merged the audit (`362480c8`, run 39814921515) ran the full
set. Its report is in `records/362480c8…/audit/39814921515-1/`.
- The audit job took 3 minutes 44 seconds, the self-test included. That is
  why pushes run `full`.
- 516 targets were fetched at their pins, none unavailable; 18,498 target

# The similarity audit

This repository says its firmware was written clean-room, without the FM-1's
GPL community firmwares (CONTRIBUTING.md). The audit backs that up with a
measurement. On every push to main, a CI job compares our firmware with
every FM-1 firmware repository it can find, and with an unrelated control
project, and puts the scores in the commit's record. Requirements:
R-AUDIT-1 to R-AUDIT-6 (docs/REQUIREMENTS.md).

Nobody working on this repository reads the targets. The spec side found
them from repository metadata alone. The job fetches them only inside CI,
and its logs and outputs hold scores and file names, never code. When the
job flags a pair, only an **auditor** may look (below).

## What is compared

- **Ours:** the C files under `firmware/` (`.c`, `.h`, and C++ suffixes if
  we ever have any). Assembly (`.S`) and linker scripts (`.ld`) are not
  compared: JPlag's C front end doesn't read them. `vendor/` is not ours
  and is never compared.
- **Base code:** the vendored JieLi SDK headers
  (`vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib`). JPlag drops matches with base code, so
  code that both sides took from the SDK doesn't count against us.
- **Targets:** the C and C++ files of every target (below), at its pinned
  commit. `audit/targets.json` lists the targets; `paths` limits a target
  to some of its folders.
- **The control:** the C files of `raspberrypi/pico-examples` at tag
  `sdk-2.2.0`, commit `4c3a3dc0196dd426fddd709616d0da984e027bab`
  (BSD-3-Clause; `audit/audit.json`).

## The targets, from metadata only

`tools/audit-discover.py` builds `audit/targets.json` from
`audit/discover.json`. It asks GitHub's REST API, and `git ls-remote`, for
repository names, owners, descriptions, licences, languages, fork lists and
commit and tree SHAs. It never opens a target's files, README or web pages,
and never prints a description. A target is:

- **a seed:** Felucca (`hugelton/Felucca`), dinghy (`zvenson/dinghy`), the
  `fm1-sid/` and `probes/` folders of fm1-emu
  (`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu`), M-VAVE's `m-vave/fm1_open`, and the other
  FM-1 repositories of Felucca's author (`felucca-bsp`,
  `Felucca-Engines`, `Felucca-WebApp`, `felucca-mirror`);
- **a search hit:** a repository that one of the search queries finds and
  whose description names the FM-1, Felucca, GHOULBOX or Hortator. A
  repository that only matches by name must also be written in C or C++.
  "M-VAVE" or "dinghy" alone don't count, because they also name other
  products, boats and tools. dinghy's own lineage is found through its
  fork tree, and through descriptions that name the FM-1;
- **any fork of a target, to any depth.** A fork inherits its parent's
  `paths` and licence override.

**As found on 2026-10-22:** 780 repositories, after two passes whose
search results differed a little. Of these, 516 are scored and 262 are
duplicates by tree. The other 2 are empty. Of the 516 scored, 381 are classed `gpl`, 47
`permissive`, 43 `other` and 45 `none`.

The owner chose this wide net on 2026-10-22: every FM-1 repository, not
only Felucca's and dinghy's lineage. A target that turns out to be
unrelated costs only CI minutes. A target that is missed weakens the
claim.

Each target is **pinned** at its default branch's head commit, together
with that commit's tree. The job checks both. Targets whose tree (and
`paths`) is already in the list are marked `duplicate` and not fetched
again. Seeds come first, then other repositories, then forks, so a fork
that changed nothing is covered by the repository it copies. Empty
repositories are listed as `empty`.

Each target's **licence** is classed from its metadata as `gpl` (GPL,
LGPL, AGPL), `permissive` (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, WTFPL, CC0 and
similar), `other` (MPL-2.0, NOASSERTION, anything else) or `none` (no
licence). fm1-emu's metadata says MIT, but `fm1-sid/` is a GPL firmware
(docs/EXPOSURE.md), so that seed is classed `gpl`. The report shows each
target's class beside its scores. A flagged pair fails the job whatever
the licence.

**Unresolved:** *Felucca Salt* and *Felucca 8 Patterns*, both named in
CONTRIBUTING.md's forbidden list. No repository for either was found from
metadata on 2026-10-22; they may be distributed only as binaries. They are
listed in `discover.json` and in every report, and the owner adds a URL if
one turns up.

**Limits:** only the default branch is pinned; work on other branches,
and code in git submodules, is not fetched. A repository that neither
search finds nor any target's fork tree reaches is missed. Repositories
deleted after pinning are reported as `not fetched`.

### Rediscovery

`.github/workflows/audit-discover.yml` runs on the first day of every month,
and on demand. It runs `tools/audit-discover.py --write`, which uses
metadata only, as above. If any target is new, gone or has moved to a new
commit, it opens an issue titled "audit: the targets have changed" that
lists those repositories by name, or updates that issue if one is still
open. The rewritten `audit/targets.json` is kept as the run's `targets`
artifact for 90 days. The job has read access to the code and write
access to issues only: it cannot push a branch or open a pull request. It
never fetches a target's code: only the audit job does that.

Search results vary from run to run, so a target already in
`targets.json` stays even when this month's searches miss it. It is
dropped only when `git ls-remote` can no longer reach its repository. A
run also reuses the stored tree of every target whose head hasn't moved, so
only new or moved repositories cost an API request for their tree. When
GitHub's rate limit runs out, it waits for the reset time GitHub gives.
Each run prints how many requests it made.

New repository names can trip the separation check (C-SEP-TERMS), as
`audit/targets.json` already did once: a repository named after another
M-VAVE keyboard that the emulator also models. In principle they could
trip the privacy check (C-PRIVATE) too. A spec-side session reviews such a
hit. A separation hit gets an entry by hash in
`config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`; a privacy hit goes to the owner.

A spec-side session turns the issue into a pull request:
1. Download the newest run's artifact, as the issue says
   (`gh run download <run> -n targets`), and replace `audit/targets.json`
   with it. Don't rerun the discovery locally: search results vary, and the
   artifact is what the issue lists.
2. Do the review just described for any separation or privacy hit.
3. Open the pull request with "Closes #<issue>". Because a person opens it,
   `ci` runs as usual, and the owner merges it with the button.

## The method

JPlag 6.3.0 (the jar with dependencies, checked against its SHA-256 in
`audit/audit.json`) runs in the Java 25 image `eclipse-temurin`, pinned by
digest, with no network. Its settings:
- the C language module, with JPlag's default minimum match of 12 tokens;
- **every file is its own submission**, because JPlag drops a whole
  submission when one of its files fails to parse;
- our files and the control's files are the "new" submissions, and the
  target files are the "old" ones. JPlag compares every new file with every
  old one, and never compares two old ones;
- each target file is scored **once per blob**: forks share most files, and
  a report lists every target and path that holds a flagged blob;
- comparisons with no match at all are not written (`-m 0.000001`), which
  loses no score.

Each file pair gets three numbers:
- the **longest match**: the longest run of tokens the two files share;
- **max**: the matched tokens over the smaller file's tokens;
- **avg**: the matched tokens over the mean of the two files' tokens.

JPlag compares token structure, not names, so renaming identifiers does
not hide a copy.

### Why the longest match, not the ratio

Before choosing, the spec side scored the control against an unrelated
permissive embedded project: TinyUSB's `src/` at commit
`3fa7b06d284c0ac1d1078a0a2d09dceb405499e7` (MIT), 244 control files against
190 TinyUSB files, 27,492 file pairs, with the same settings. Nothing
GPL was involved.

| Score | Median | 99th percentile | 99.9th percentile | Highest |
|-------|--------|-----------------|-------------------|---------|
| Longest match (tokens) | 0 | 13 | 17 | 33 |
| max (ratio) | 0 | 0.116 | 0.325 | 0.857 |

The ratio reaches 0.857 between two unrelated projects: a short file is
easily "mostly matched" by chance. The longest match stays short between
unrelated code, while a copied function gives one long run. So the gate
uses the longest match, and the report shows `max` and `avg` beside it.

### The threshold

The job **fails** when a pair of one of our files and a target file has a
longest match above the **threshold**:

> threshold = the control's longest match with any target it is not
> related to + 24 tokens

The control's highest score is what chance gives, in this run, against
these targets. That covers code idioms, common libraries and headers the
targets share with any embedded C. The margin of 24 tokens is twice
JPlag's minimum match: three or four C statements of identical structure,
beyond the longest run that unrelated embedded code shares with any
target. The calibration's highest chance run was 33 tokens, so the
threshold works out at about 55 to 60 tokens: six to eight lines of the
same code, which chance did not produce once in 27,492 pairs.

**Control-related targets.** A target that the control itself matches by
more than **100 tokens** is not unrelated to it. Some FM-1 repository might
carry Raspberry Pi code, for example a recovery tool for a Pico. Such a
target:
- is listed in the report as *control-related*;
- is left out of the baseline, so it doesn't raise the threshold for every
  other target;
- is judged against the control's own score there: a pair of ours fails
  above that score plus 24.

A file that several targets hold gets the strictest of their thresholds.
C-AUDIT-CONTROL fails if more than 10% of the scored targets are
control-related. The control would then be a poor yardstick for these
targets, and the owner chooses another, by pull request. A dry run showed
why this rule is needed. Against TinyUSB as a whole (not only its `src/`),
the control shares a 107-token run, because TinyUSB's own Raspberry Pi port
overlaps pico-examples' USB examples. One target like that would otherwise
have lifted the threshold for all of them.

### What the gate cannot see

- **Small files.** A pair can fail only if its longest match is above the
  threshold. A verbatim copy of a file shorter than the threshold therefore
  can't fail the job. Today our files are 54, 20 and 16 tokens long, so an
  exact copy of one of them would show as a top pair with `max` 1.0 but
  would not fail the job. The report lists each of our files' token counts,
  and its top pairs with `max`, so a reader can see this. The gate gets
  stronger as the firmware grows.
- **Drift.** The control is fixed and the firmware grows. Larger files have
  more chances to share a run by accident. The control's score, measured
  against the same targets in the same run, is the yardstick. If the
  firmware ever dwarfs the control, a larger control is chosen, by pull
  request.
- **Reordered or rewritten code** splits a copied run into shorter ones.
  Clean-room work is meant to prevent that kind of derivation, and the audit
  is evidence for it, not proof.

### Why this control

`raspberrypi/pico-examples` is:
- permissive (BSD-3-Clause);
- pinned at a release tag;
- embedded C of the same kind as ours: startup and clocks, timers,
  interrupts, UART, GPIO, DMA, audio and display examples;
- mostly small files, as ours are.

It is written for a different chip family (RP2040 and RP2350) and has
nothing to do with the FM-1, so its similarity to the targets is chance
and shared idiom, not copying. Its scores measure the noise floor that ours
are judged against. TinyUSB, used for the calibration above, was not chosen
as the control: an FM-1 firmware could reasonably vendor TinyUSB for USB

88	def fetch(url, commit, tree, dest, suffixes, paths=None):
89	    """The commit's C/C++ files (blob-less, depth 1, sparse) in dest.
90	    Returns [(blob, path)] of the files on disk."""
91	    os.makedirs(dest)
92	    git(["init", "-q"], dest)
93	    if git(["fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--filter=blob:none", url, commit], dest).returncode:
94	        raise Unavailable("could not fetch the pinned commit")
95	    got = git(["rev-parse", "FETCH_HEAD^{tree}"], dest).stdout.decode().strip()
96	    if tree and got != tree:
97	        raise Mismatch("tree %s, pinned %s" % (got[:12], tree[:12]))
98	    ls = git(["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "FETCH_HEAD"], dest).stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
99	    files = []
100	    for rec in ls.split("\0"):
101	        meta, _, path = rec.partition("\t")
102	        parts = meta.split()
103	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1] == "blob" and parts[0] != "120000" and wanted(path, suffixes, paths):
104	            files.append((parts[2], path))
105	    if not files:
106	        return []
107	    pats = []
108	    for p in (paths or [""]):
109	        for s in suffixes:
110	            for v in {s, s.upper()}:
111	                pats.append(("/" + p + "**/*" + v) if p else ("*" + v))
112	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "sparse-checkout", "set", "--no-cone", "--stdin"], cwd=dest,
113	                       input="\n".join(pats).encode(), stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=GIT_ENV)
114	    if p.returncode or git(["checkout", "-q", "FETCH_HEAD"], dest).returncode:
115	        raise Unavailable("could not check out the pinned commit's files")
116	    return [(b, path) for b, path in files if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(dest, path))]

119	class Pool:
120	    """Target files, one copy per blob: pool/p00001.c ..., and where each came from."""
121	
122	    def __init__(self, folder):
123	        self.dir = folder
124	        os.makedirs(folder)
125	        self.by_blob = {}
126	        self.where = {}
127	
128	    def add(self, blob, src, repo, path):
129	        new = blob not in self.by_blob
130	        if new:
131	            name = "p%05d%s" % (len(self.by_blob) + 1, os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower())
132	            shutil.copyfile(src, os.path.join(self.dir, name))
133	            self.by_blob[blob] = name
134	            self.where[name] = []
135	        name = self.by_blob[blob]
136	        self.where[name].append((repo, path))
137	        return name, new

140	def copy_tree_files(top, suffixes, dest, prefix):
141	    """Our files (or the control's): dest/<prefix>00001.c ..., and a map to their paths."""
142	    names = {}
143	    for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(top):
144	        dirs[:] = sorted(d for d in dirs if d != ".git")
145	        for f in sorted(files):
146	            full = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
147	            rel = os.path.relpath(full, top).replace(os.sep, "/")
148	            if wanted(rel, suffixes) and os.path.isfile(full):
149	                name = "%s%05d%s" % (prefix, len(names) + 1, os.path.splitext(f)[1].lower())
150	                shutil.copyfile(full, os.path.join(dest, name))
151	                names[name] = rel
152	    return names

176	def read_results(path):
177	    """Names and numbers from JPlag's report archive: comparisons, failed submissions, token counts."""
178	    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
179	        top = json.loads(z.read("topComparisons.json"))
180	        info = json.loads(z.read("runInformation.json"))
181	        index = json.loads(z.read("submissionFileIndex.json"))
182	    pairs = []
183	    for c in top:
184	        a, b = sub(c["firstSubmission"]), sub(c["secondSubmission"])
185	        s = c["similarities"]
186	        if a and b:
187	            pairs.append((a, b, int(s.get("LONGEST_MATCH", 0)), float(s.get("MAX", 0)), float(s.get("AVG", 0))))
188	    failed = {}
189	    for f in info.get("failedSubmissions", []):
190	        n = sub(f.get("submissionId", ""))
191	        if n:
192	            failed[n] = f.get("submissionState", "FAILED")
193	    tokens = {}
194	    for k, v in index.get("fileIndexes", {}).items():
195	        n = sub(k)
196	        if n:
197	            tokens[n] = sum(int(x.get("tokenCount", 0)) for x in v.values())
198	    return pairs, failed, tokens

206	def score(pairs, cfg, where):
207	    """Splits JPlag's pairs by kind and applies the gate. Pairs are
208	    (a, b, longest, max, avg) with a and b named o.. (ours), c.. (control)
209	    or p.. (a target file); where maps a target file to its (repo, path)s.
210	
211	    The baseline is the control's longest match with any target it is not
212	    related to; a target the control itself matches above the ceiling is
213	    control-related, and is judged against the control's own score there.
214	    A pair of ours fails above its target's score plus the margin (for a
215	    file several targets hold, the strictest of theirs)."""
216	    ours, ctl, ours_ctl = [], [], []
217	    for a, b, l, m, v in pairs:
218	        k = {a[0], b[0]}
219	        if k == {"o", "p"}:
220	            o, p = (a, b) if a[0] == "o" else (b, a)
221	            ours.append((o, p, l, m, v))
222	        elif k == {"c", "p"}:
223	            c, p = (a, b) if a[0] == "c" else (b, a)
224	            ctl.append((c, p, l, m, v))
225	        elif k == {"o", "c"}:
226	            o, c = (a, b) if a[0] == "o" else (b, a)
227	            ours_ctl.append((o, c, l, m, v))
228	    best = lambda xs: sorted(xs, key=lambda x: (-x[2], -x[3], x[0], x[1]))
229	    per_target = {}
230	    for c, p, l, m, v in ctl:
231	        for repo, _ in where.get(p, []):
232	            per_target[repo] = max(per_target.get(repo, 0), l)
233	    related = sorted(r for r, l in per_target.items() if l > cfg["control_ceiling_tokens"])
234	    baseline = max([l for r, l in per_target.items() if r not in related], default=0)
235	
236	    def threshold(p):
237	        return min([(per_target[r] if r in related else baseline) + cfg["margin_tokens"]
238	                    for r, _ in where.get(p, [])] or [baseline + cfg["margin_tokens"]])
239	
240	    flagged = [x for x in best(ours) if x[2] > threshold(x[1])]
241	    return {"ours": best(ours), "control": best(ctl), "ours_control": best(ours_ctl),
242	            "control_max": baseline, "threshold": baseline + cfg["margin_tokens"], "flagged": flagged,
243	            "related": related, "control_per_target": per_target}
244

246	def split_accepted(rows, rules):
247	    """Flagged pairs an auditor's finding accepted (audit/accepted.json: our
248	    file, the target's repo and path, the longest match accepted, the
249	    finding) are moved out of the gate while their score stays at or below
250	    the accepted one; a place not covered keeps the pair flagged."""
251	    flagged, accepted = [], []
252	    for row in rows:
253	        def ok(t):
254	            return any(r["ours"] == row["ours"] and r["repo"] == t["repo"] and r["path"] == t["path"]
255	                       and row["longest_tokens"] <= r["longest_tokens"] for r in rules)
256	        if row["target_places"] == len(row["target_files"]) and row["target_files"] and all(ok(t) for t in row["target_files"]):
257	            accepted.append(dict(row, findings=sorted(set(r["finding"] for r in rules if r["ours"] == row["ours"]))))
258	        else:
259	            flagged.append(row)
260	    return flagged, accepted

275	def leak(texts, folder, min_chars):
276	    """The name of a file in folder one of whose lines (stripped, at least
277	    min_chars long) occurs in texts, or None."""
278	    joined = "\n".join(texts)
279	    windows = set(joined[i:i + min_chars] for i in range(max(0, len(joined) - min_chars + 1)))
280	    for name in sorted(os.listdir(folder)):
281	        with open(os.path.join(folder, name), "rb") as f:
282	            text = f.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
283	        for line in text.splitlines():
284	            s = line.strip()
285	            if len(s) >= min_chars and s[:min_chars] in windows and s in joined:
286	                return name
287	    return None

299	def run(cfg, targets_doc, set_name, out, jar=None, selftest=None):
300	    """One audit. selftest: a list of target dicts used instead of targets_doc's."""
301	    t0 = time.time()
302	    checks = {}
303	    base_tmp = os.environ.get("RUNNER_TEMP") or None
304	    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="audit-", dir=base_tmp)
305	    report = {"schema": SCHEMA, "set": set_name, "commit": os.environ.get("GITHUB_SHA") or
306	              git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], ROOT).stdout.decode().strip(),
307	              "run": ("%s/%s/actions/runs/%s" % (os.environ["GITHUB_SERVER_URL"], os.environ["GITHUB_REPOSITORY"],
308	                                                os.environ["GITHUB_RUN_ID"]) if os.environ.get("GITHUB_RUN_ID") else None),
309	              "jplag": {"version": cfg["jplag"]["version"], "sha256": cfg["jplag"]["sha256"]},
310	              "java_image": cfg["java_image"], "margin_tokens": cfg["margin_tokens"],
311	              "control_ceiling_tokens": cfg["control_ceiling_tokens"], "min_tokens": cfg["min_tokens"]}
312	    try:
313	        for d in ("new", "base"):
314	            os.makedirs(os.path.join(work, d))
315	        jar_path, got = get_jar(cfg, work, jar)
316	        jar_ok = got == cfg["jplag"]["sha256"] and "@sha256:" in cfg["java_image"]
317	        checks["C-AUDIT-JPLAG"] = ("PASS" if jar_ok else "FAIL",
318	                                   "jar sha256 %s; Java image pinned by digest" % ("matches" if jar_ok else "differs: " + got))
319	        if not jar_ok:
320	            raise RuntimeError("JPlag is not the pinned jar")
321	        ours = copy_tree_files(os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["ours"]), cfg["suffixes"], os.path.join(work, "new"), "o")
322	        for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["base_code"])):
323	            for f in files:
324	                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["base_code"]))
325	                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.join(work, "base", rel)), exist_ok=True)
326	                shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(work, "base", rel))
327	        c = cfg["control"]
328	        ctl_dir = os.path.join(work, "control")
329	        problems = []
330	        try:
331	            fetch(c["url"], c["commit"], c["tree"], ctl_dir, cfg["suffixes"])
332	        except (Unavailable, Mismatch) as e:
333	            problems.append("control %s: %s" % (c["repo"], e))
334	        control = copy_tree_files(ctl_dir, cfg["suffixes"], os.path.join(work, "new"), "c")
335	        shutil.rmtree(ctl_dir, ignore_errors=True)
336	        report["control"] = {"repo": c["repo"], "commit": c["commit"], "licence": c["licence"], "files": len(control)}
337	
338	        all_targets = selftest if selftest is not None else targets_doc["targets"]
339	        chosen = [t for t in all_targets if t.get("status") == "scored" and (set_name != "fast" or t["repo"] in cfg["fast"])]
340	        pool = Pool(os.path.join(work, "pool"))
341	        licences = {t["repo"]: t.get("licence_class", "none") for t in all_targets}
342	        rows = []
343	
344	        def fetch_one(i, t):
345	            tdir = os.path.join(work, "t%05d" % i)
346	            try:
347	                url = t["url"] if selftest is not None else t["url"] + ".git"
348	                return tdir, fetch(url, t["commit"], t.get("tree"), tdir, cfg["suffixes"], t.get("paths")), None
349	            except (Unavailable, Mismatch) as e:
350	                return tdir, None, e
351	
352	        # fetched side by side, but added to the pool in the list's order, so its names are stable
353	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=cfg.get("fetch_workers", 8)) as ex:
354	            futures = [ex.submit(fetch_one, i, t) for i, t in enumerate(chosen)]
355	            for t, fut in zip(chosen, futures):
356	                tdir, files, err = fut.result()
357	                row = {"repo": t["repo"], "commit": t["commit"], "licence": t.get("licence"),
358	                       "licence_class": t.get("licence_class", "none")}
359	                if err is None:
360	                    new = 0
361	                    for blob, path in files:
362	                        _, is_new = pool.add(blob, os.path.join(tdir, path), t["repo"], path)
363	                        new += is_new
364	                    row.update({"fetched": True, "files": len(files), "new_files": new})
365	                elif isinstance(err, Mismatch):
366	                    row.update({"fetched": False, "why": "tree mismatch: " + str(err)})
367	                    problems.append("%s: tree mismatch" % t["repo"])
368	                else:
369	                    row.update({"fetched": False, "why": str(err)})
370	                shutil.rmtree(tdir, ignore_errors=True)
371	                rows.append(row)
372	        unavailable = [r["repo"] for r in rows if not r["fetched"] and not r.get("why", "").startswith("tree")]
373	        checks["C-AUDIT-PIN"] = ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS",
374	                                 "%d targets fetched at their pinned commit and tree; %d unavailable%s"
375	                                 % (sum(r["fetched"] for r in rows), len(unavailable),
376	                                    ("; " + "; ".join(problems)) if problems else ""))
377	        report["targets"] = rows
378	        if targets_doc and selftest is None:
379	            report["unresolved"] = [u["name"] for u in targets_doc.get("unresolved", [])]
380	            report["not_scored"] = {s: sum(1 for t in all_targets if t.get("status") == s)
381	                                    for s in ("duplicate", "empty", "unreachable")}
382	        report["pool_files"] = len(pool.where)
383	
384	        if not pool.where:
385	            raise RuntimeError("no target files were fetched")
386	        code = run_jplag(cfg, work)
387	        result = os.path.join(work, "result.jplag")
388	        if code or not os.path.exists(result):
389	            raise RuntimeError("JPlag failed (exit %d); its log is not shown, as it can quote the files" % code)
390	        pairs, failed, tokens = read_results(result)
391	        os.remove(result)
392	        s = score(pairs, cfg, pool.where)
393	        names = dict(ours)
394	        names.update(control)
395	        # JPlag leaves a file that matched nothing (no run of min_tokens) out
396	        # of its index, so its token count is unknown; it was still compared.
397	        report["ours_files"] = [{"file": p, "tokens": tokens.get(n), "state": failed.get(n, "scored" if n in tokens else "no match")}
398	                                for n, p in sorted(ours.items())]
399	        report["control_max_tokens"] = s["control_max"]
400	        report["threshold_tokens"] = s["threshold"]
401	        report["top_pairs"] = [pair_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences) for x in s["ours"][:cfg["top_pairs"]]]
402	        report["control_top_pairs"] = [pair_row(x, control, pool.where, licences) for x in s["control"][:5]]
403	        report["ours_vs_control_best"] = ([{"ours": ours.get(x[0]), "control": control.get(x[1]), "longest_tokens": x[2],
404	                                            "max": round(x[3], 4)} for x in s["ours_control"][:3]])
405	        by_repo_ours, by_repo_ctl = {}, s["control_per_target"]
406	        for x in s["ours"]:
407	            for r, _ in pool.where.get(x[1], []):
408	                by_repo_ours[r] = max(by_repo_ours.get(r, 0), x[2])
409	        unparsed = {}
410	        for n, state in failed.items():
411	            for r, _ in pool.where.get(n, []):
412	                unparsed.setdefault(r, {}).setdefault(state.lower(), 0)
413	                unparsed[r][state.lower()] += 1
414	        for row in rows:
415	            row["ours_longest_tokens"] = by_repo_ours.get(row["repo"], 0)
416	            row["control_longest_tokens"] = by_repo_ctl.get(row["repo"], 0)
417	            row["not_parsed"] = unparsed.get(row["repo"], {})
418	        accepted_rules = load_json(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "accepted.json")).get("accepted", []) \
419	            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "accepted.json")) else []
420	        flagged, accepted = split_accepted([pair_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences, limit=None) for x in s["flagged"]],
421	                                           accepted_rules)
422	        s["flagged"] = flagged
423	        report["flagged"] = flagged
424	        report["accepted"] = accepted
425	        report["control_related"] = s["related"]
426	        fetched = sum(r["fetched"] for r in rows)
427	        ctl_ok = bool(control) and len(s["related"]) <= cfg["control_related_share"] * max(fetched, 1)
428	        checks["C-AUDIT-CONTROL"] = ("PASS" if ctl_ok else "FAIL",
429	                                     "%d control files; its longest match with an unrelated target %d tokens; "
430	                                     "%d of %d targets control-related (above %d tokens; at most %d%% allowed)"
431	                                     % (len(control), s["control_max"], len(s["related"]), fetched,
432	                                        cfg["control_ceiling_tokens"], round(100 * cfg["control_related_share"])))
433	        checks["C-AUDIT-SCORE"] = ("FAIL" if s["flagged"] else "PASS",
434	                                   "%d of our file pairs above %d tokens (the control's %d plus %d; for a "
435	                                   "control-related target, its own score plus %d)%s"
436	                                   % (len(s["flagged"]), s["threshold"], s["control_max"], cfg["margin_tokens"],
437	                                      cfg["margin_tokens"],
438	                                      "; %d more accepted by an auditor's finding" % len(accepted) if accepted else ""))
439	        if selftest is not None:
440	            report["selftest"] = {"ours_best": [[ours.get(x[0], x[0])] + list(x[1:]) for x in s["ours"]]}
441	        report["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
442	        write_report(report, checks, out, pool.dir, cfg)
443	    except Exception as e:  # the report says what failed; nothing from the targets is printed
444	        checks.setdefault("C-AUDIT-SCORE", ("FAIL", "not scored: %s" % e))
445	        report["error"] = str(e)
446	        report["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
447	        pool_dir = os.path.join(work, "pool")
448	        write_report(report, checks, out, pool_dir if os.path.isdir(pool_dir) else None, cfg)
449	    finally:
450	        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
451	    gone = not os.path.exists(work)
452	    print("temporary folder removed: %s" % ("yes" if gone else "NO"))
453	    return report, checks

460	        res = [checks[c][0] for c in mine]

462	                      "result": "FAIL" if "FAIL" in res else "PASS" if res else "not run"})

466	def write_report(report, checks, out, pool_dir, cfg):
467	    report["checks"] = [{"id": k, "result": v[0], "detail": v[1], "reqs": REQS[k]} for k, v in checks.items()]
468	    report["traceability"] = traceability(checks)
469	    md = markdown(report)
470	    text = json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
471	    if pool_dir:
472	        hit = leak([md] + list(report_strings(report)), pool_dir, cfg["leak_line_chars"])
473	        report["checks"].append({"id": "C-AUDIT-LEAK", "result": "FAIL" if hit else "PASS", "reqs": REQS["C-AUDIT-LEAK"],
474	                                 "detail": "a line of a target file is in the report; report withheld" if hit else
475	                                 "no line of a target file (%d characters or more) in the report" % cfg["leak_line_chars"]})
476	        if hit:
477	            report = {k: report[k] for k in ("schema", "set", "commit", "run", "checks")}
478	        report["traceability"] = traceability({c["id"]: (c["result"], "") for c in report["checks"]})
479	        md = markdown(report)
480	        text = json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
481	    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
482	    with open(os.path.join(out, "report.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
483	        f.write(text + "\n")
484	    with open(os.path.join(out, "report.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
485	        f.write(md)
486	
487	
488	def markdown(r):
489	    L = ["# Similarity audit %s" % (r.get("commit") or "")[:12], "",
490	         "- Set: %s; run: %s" % (r.get("set"), r.get("run") or "local"),
491	         "- JPlag %s (sha256 `%s`), Java image `%s`" % (r.get("jplag", {}).get("version"),
492	                                                        r.get("jplag", {}).get("sha256", "")[:16], r.get("java_image", "")),
493	         ""]
494	    if "threshold_tokens" in r:
495	        L += ["- Control: %s at `%s`, %s files" % (r["control"]["repo"], r["control"]["commit"][:12], r["control"]["files"]),
496	              "- The control's longest match with any target it is not related to: **%d tokens**; a pair of ours "
497	              "fails above **%d tokens** (margin %d)." % (r["control_max_tokens"], r["threshold_tokens"], r["margin_tokens"]),
498	              "- Control-related targets (the control matches them above %d tokens; each judged against the "
499	              "control's own score there plus the margin): %s" % (r["control_ceiling_tokens"],
500	                                                                  ", ".join(r.get("control_related", [])) or "none"),
501	              "- Target files scored: %d (one copy per blob)" % r.get("pool_files", 0), ""]
502	    if r.get("error"):
503	        L += ["**Not scored:** %s" % r["error"], ""]
504	    L += ["## Checks", "", "| Check | Result | Detail |", "|---|---|---|"]
505	    for c in r.get("checks", []):
506	        L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
507	    if r.get("flagged"):
508	        L += ["", "## Flagged pairs (an auditor compares these; nobody else opens them)", "",
509	              "| Our file | Target | Path | Licence | Longest | Max |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
510	        for p in r["flagged"]:
511	            for t in p["target_files"]:
512	                L.append("| %s | %s | %s | %s | %d | %.3f |" % (p["ours"], t["repo"], t["path"], t["licence_class"],
513	                                                               p["longest_tokens"], p["max"]))
514	    if "top_pairs" in r and not r["top_pairs"]:
515	        L += ["", "## Our top file pairs", "", "None: no file of ours shares a run of %d tokens or more with any target file."
516	              % r.get("min_tokens", 12)]
517	    if r.get("top_pairs"):
518	        L += ["", "## Our top file pairs", "", "| Our file | Target (places with this file) | Path | Licence | Longest | Max | Avg |",
519	              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
520	        for p in r["top_pairs"]:
521	            t = p["target_files"][0] if p["target_files"] else {"repo": "?", "path": "?", "licence_class": "?"}
522	            L.append("| %s | %s (%d) | %s | %s | %d | %.3f | %.3f |" % (p["ours"], t["repo"], p["target_places"], t["path"],
523	                                                                     t["licence_class"], p["longest_tokens"], p["max"], p["avg"]))
524	    if r.get("ours_files"):
525	        L += ["", "## Our files", "", "| File | Tokens | State |", "|---|---|---|"]
526	        for f in r["ours_files"]:
527	            L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (f["file"], f["tokens"] if f["tokens"] is not None else "-", f["state"]))
528	    if r.get("targets"):
529	        L += ["", "## Targets", "", "| Target | Commit | Licence | Files (new) | Ours longest | Control longest | Not parsed |",
530	              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
531	        for t in r["targets"]:
532	            if t.get("fetched"):
533	                np = ", ".join("%s %d" % kv for kv in sorted(t.get("not_parsed", {}).items())) or "0"
534	                L.append("| %s | `%s` | %s | %d (%d) | %s | %s | %s |" % (
535	                    t["repo"], t["commit"][:12], t["licence_class"], t["files"], t["new_files"],
536	                    t.get("ours_longest_tokens", "-"), t.get("control_longest_tokens", "-"), np))
537	            else:
538	                L.append("| %s | `%s` | %s | not fetched: %s | | | |" % (t["repo"], t["commit"][:12], t["licence_class"], t.get("why")))
539	    if "not_scored" in r:
540	        L += ["", "Not scored: %s. Unresolved (no repository found): %s." % (
541	            ", ".join("%d %s" % (v, k) for k, v in r["not_scored"].items()), ", ".join(r.get("unresolved", [])) or "none")]
542	    L += ["", "## Traceability", "", "| Requirement | Checks | Result |", "|---|---|---|"]
543	    for t in r.get("traceability", []):
544	        L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (t["requirement"], ", ".join(t["checks"]), t["result"]))
545	    L.append("")
546	    return "\n".join(L)
547	
548	
549	def selftest_target(work_parent, cfg):
550	    """A made-up local target: verbatim copies of our files and one unrelated
551	    file, in a git repository served by path. Returns (target dict, its folder)."""
552	    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="audit-selftest-", dir=work_parent)
553	    src = os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["ours"])
554	    for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(src):
555	        for f in files:
556	            if wanted(f, cfg["suffixes"]):
557	                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, f), src)
558	                os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "copied", os.path.dirname(rel)), exist_ok=True)
559	                shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(d, "copied", rel))
560	    with open(os.path.join(d, "unrelated.c"), "w") as f:
561	        f.write("int unrelated(int a) { return a * 3 + 1; }\n")
562	    env = dict(GIT_ENV, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="[REDACTED:email]",
563	               GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="[REDACTED:email]")
564	    for args in (["init", "-q"], ["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-q", "-m", "selftest"],
565	                 ["config", "uploadpack.allowFilter", "true"], ["config", "uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant", "true"]):
566	        subprocess.run(["git"] + args, cwd=d, check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env)
567	    commit = git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], d).stdout.decode().strip()
568	    tree = git(["rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}"], d).stdout.decode().strip()
569	    return {"repo": "selftest/copy-of-ours", "url": "file://" + d, "commit": commit, "tree": tree,
570	            "status": "scored", "licence_class": "none"}, d
571	
572	
573	def selftest_verdict(report):
574	    """Every one of our files must be scored and found in the made-up target
575	    with a match covering at least 90% of its tokens, and the report written."""
576	    files = report.get("ours_files", [])
577	    tokens = {f["file"]: f["tokens"] for f in files if f["state"] == "scored"}
578	    best = {}
579	    for o, p, l, m, v in report.get("selftest", {}).get("ours_best", []):
580	        best[o] = max(best.get(o, 0), l)
581	    found = [f for f, t in tokens.items() if best.get(f, 0) >= 0.9 * t]
582	    leak_ok = any(c["id"] == "C-AUDIT-LEAK" and c["result"] == "PASS" for c in report.get("checks", []))
583	    ok = bool(files) and len(found) == len(files) and leak_ok
584	    return ok, "%d of our %d files found in a target holding copies of them; leak check %s" % (
585	        len(found), len(files), "PASS" if leak_ok else "not passed")
586	
587	
588	def check_artifact(folder):
589	    names = sorted(os.listdir(folder))
590	    if names != ["report.json", "report.md"]:
591	        return ["unexpected files: %s" % names]
592	    problems = []
593	    for n in names:
594	        if os.path.getsize(os.path.join(folder, n)) > 2 << 20:
595	            problems.append("%s is too large" % n)
596	    r = load_json(os.path.join(folder, "report.json"))
597	    if r.get("schema") != SCHEMA or not isinstance(r.get("checks"), list):
598	        problems.append("report.json is not an audit report")
599	    return problems
600	
601	
602	def main(argv=None):
603	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
604	    ap.add_argument("command", choices=["run", "selftest", "check-artifact"])
605	    ap.add_argument("dir", nargs="?")
606	    ap.add_argument("--set", default="full", choices=["full", "fast"])
607	    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "audit"))
608	    ap.add_argument("--jar")
609	    ap.add_argument("--config", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "audit.json"))
610	    ap.add_argument("--targets", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "targets.json"))
611	    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
612	    if a.command == "check-artifact":
613	        problems = check_artifact(a.dir)
614	        for p in problems:
615	            print("FAIL %s" % p)
616	        print("artifact: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
617	        return 1 if problems else 0
618	    cfg = load_json(a.config)
619	    if a.command == "selftest":
620	        t, d = selftest_target(os.environ.get("RUNNER_TEMP") or None, cfg)
621	        try:
622	            report, checks = run(cfg, None, "selftest", a.out, a.jar, selftest=[t])
623	        finally:
624	            shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
625	        ok, detail = selftest_verdict(report)
626	        print("C-AUDIT-SELFTEST: %s (%s)" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", detail))
627	        for c in report.get("checks", []):
628	            print("  %s %s: %s" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
629	        return 0 if ok else 1
630	    report, checks = run(cfg, load_json(a.targets), a.set, a.out, a.jar)
631	    for c in report.get("checks", []):
632	        print("%s %s: %s" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
633	    failed = [c["id"] for c in report.get("checks", []) if c["result"] != "PASS"]
634	    print("audit: %s" % ("FAIL (%s)" % ", ".join(failed) if failed else "PASS"))
635	    return 1 if failed else 0
636	
637	
638	if __name__ == "__main__":
639	    sys.exit(main())

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# The similarity audit (R-AUDIT-1 to R-AUDIT-5; docs/AUDIT.md). Runs for
# pushes to main and on demand, never for pull requests (there is no such
# trigger, and both jobs also require main).
#
# Job `audit` is the only place the GPL targets ever exist: it has read-only
# permissions, no environment and no secrets. tools/audit.py fetches each
# target at its pinned commit into a temporary folder, scores it with JPlag
# (whose own output is never shown) and deletes it; nothing is cached. The
# job uploads only report.json and report.md: scores and file names.
#
# Job `record` never sees the targets. It checks that the artifact holds
# only that report and appends it to the commit's record on the `records`
# branch, as records/<sha>/audit/<run>-<attempt>/, with the records
# environment's deploy key.
name: audit

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      set:
        description: "full: every target; fast: Felucca, dinghy, fm1-emu's fm1-sid, fm1_open"
        type: choice
        options: [full, fast]
        default: full

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: audit
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  audit:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 120
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Fetch JPlag (tools/audit.py checks its SHA-256)
        run: |
          url=$(python -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("audit/audit.json"))["jplag"]["url"])')
          curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/jplag.jar" "$url"

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest
import zipfile

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

audit = load_tool("audit.py")
disc = load_tool("audit-discover.py")
CFG = {"margin_tokens": 24, "control_ceiling_tokens": 100, "control_related_share": 0.1, "leak_line_chars": 24}


class DiscoverTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-AUDIT-2"""

    def test_licence_classes(self):
        for spdx, cls in (("GPL-3.0", "gpl"), ("AGPL-3.0", "gpl"), ("LGPL-2.1", "gpl"), ("MIT", "permissive"),
                          ("BSD-3-Clause", "permissive"), ("WTFPL", "permissive"), ("MPL-2.0", "other"),
                          ("NOASSERTION", "other"), (None, "none")):
            self.assertEqual(disc.licence_class(spdx), cls, spdx)

    def test_dedupe_keeps_the_first_by_tree_seeds_first(self):
        ts = [{"repo": "a/fork", "fork_of": "x/up", "tree": "t1", "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "x/up", "seed": 1, "tree": "t1", "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "b/other", "tree": "t2", "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "c/fork", "fork_of": "b/other", "tree": "t2", "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "d/sub", "tree": "t1", "paths": ["sub/"], "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "e/empty", "status": "empty"}]
        got = {t["repo"]: (t["status"], t.get("same_tree_as")) for t in disc.dedupe(ts)}
        self.assertEqual(got["x/up"], ("scored", None))
        self.assertEqual(got["a/fork"], ("duplicate", "x/up"))
        self.assertEqual(got["c/fork"], ("duplicate", "b/other"))
        self.assertEqual(got["d/sub"], ("scored", None), "the same tree with other paths is scored")
        self.assertEqual(got["e/empty"], ("empty", None))

    def test_changes_name_new_gone_and_moved(self):
        old = {"targets": [{"repo": "a/a", "commit": "1"}, {"repo": "b/b", "commit": "2"}]}
        new = {"targets": [{"repo": "a/a", "commit": "9"}, {"repo": "c/c", "commit": "3"}]}
        self.assertEqual(disc.changes(old, new), (["c/c"], ["b/b"], ["a/a"]))

    def test_committed_targets_are_pinned(self):
        doc = audit.load_json(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "targets.json"))
        self.assertTrue(doc["targets"])
        for t in doc["targets"]:
            self.assertIn(t["licence_class"], ("gpl", "permissive", "other", "none"), t["repo"])
            if t["status"] in ("scored", "duplicate"):
                self.assertRegex(t["commit"], r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$", t["repo"])
                self.assertRegex(t["tree"], r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$", t["repo"])
            if t["status"] == "duplicate":
                self.assertIn(t["same_tree_as"], {x["repo"] for x in doc["targets"]})
        names = {t["repo"] for t in doc["targets"]}
        for seed in audit.load_json(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "discover.json"))["seeds"]:
            self.assertIn(seed["repo"], names)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(u["name"] for u in doc["unresolved"]), ["Felucca 8 Patterns", "Felucca Salt"])


class ScoreTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-AUDIT-1, R-AUDIT-4, R-AUDIT-5"""

    def test_names_from_jplag(self):
        self.assertEqual(audit.sub("new_o00001.c"), "o00001.c")
        self.assertEqual(audit.sub("pool/p00042.h"), "p00042.h")
        self.assertEqual(audit.sub("new/c00003.cpp"), "c00003.cpp")
        self.assertIsNone(audit.sub("other_thing.c"))

    def test_gate_is_the_control_max_plus_the_margin(self):
        where = {"p00001.c": [("a/a", "x.c")], "p00002.c": [("b/b", "y.c")], "p00003.c": [("a/a", "z.c")],
                 "p00009.c": [("b/b", "w.c")]}
        pairs = [("o00001.c", "p00001.c", 50, 0.9, 0.2),

### M2: the screen (firmware side)
- Drive the LCD from our own code: bring-up, a frame buffer sent by DMA,
  drawing, our own font, a test screen with the heartbeat on it
  (docs/prompts/M2.md).
- Requirements: R-LCD-1 to R-LCD-5; R-IRQ-1, R-IRQ-2, R-BOOT-3 and
  R-PERF-1 to R-PERF-5 amended.
- Status 2026-10-22 (session M2, firmware side, on the owner's Mac):
  - **Start** (#30): `tools/clean-update.sh` passed. M1's transcript was
    archived. The transcript check's gap was closed: a folder name ended
    by `;` or another shell operator is now matched. 22 flagged calls were
    listed in `sessions/REVIEWED.json` with the owner's approval.
    The M1 release was made from the signed tag `m1`: the image and ELF,
    rebuilt bit for bit, an SBOM and checksums, with the record linked by
    tree hash and SHA256SUMS hash.
  - **Two barrier gaps closed:**
    - `tools/reproduce` used `git archive`, which with lazy fetching on
      downloads spec-side files into a clean folder's `.git` (#30).
    - The pre-commit private-terms scan read staged spec-side files after
      a merge, which with lazy fetching on would fetch them (#34).
    - Neither fetched anything here: lazy fetching was off, and the
      barrier checks passed before and after.
  - **The speed gate, by the owner's decision** (#31): perf measures
    startup and steady state apart, from two runs (1.25 and 2.25 s). Each
    has a budget per milestone. The 3% gate applies to steady state
    between records under the same budget. M1 re-measured: startup 5 193
    instructions, steady state exactly 64.000 a period.
  - **M2 budgets** (#33): code 8 192, static RAM 122 880, stack 512,
    startup 1 572 864, steady state 72 a period (unchanged).
  - **Firmware** (#35; docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M2):
    - **Bring-up:** software reset, 120 ms, sleep out, 5 ms (waited on the
      tick), 16-bit pixels, `MADCTL` 0, the first frame with the display
      off, display on.
    - **Frame buffer:** 240 × 240 RGB565, high byte first (115 200
      bytes). Sent by DMA straight from the buffer: a whole frame is 15
      chunks of 16 rows, chained by SPI1's interrupt, below the tick in
      priority.
    - **Drawing and font:** fill, frames, lines, text, and our own font
      (printable ASCII, 5 × 8, drawn as `#`/`.` rows).
    - **Screens:** an address pattern, in which each pixel's colour
      encodes its address, then a test screen (border, corner colours,
      ramps, lines, every glyph). The heartbeat's seconds are drawn once a
      second, and only their rows sent.
    - **Found on the way:**
      - fwtest raises source 16 at the end of every DMA transfer, even with
        `CON` bit 13 clear (reported in SR-3).
      - An idle wait for a chained frame's end could sleep until the next
        tick; it now spins.
      - Startup's clearing of the frame buffer delays the time base by
        0.24 ms, so the end check's slack follows bss.
  - **Results** (local runs; the records of the merges are authoritative):
    - Every one of the 57 600 pattern pixels is right; the test screen's
      border, corners and ramps are right; the golden images match.
    - With whole frames back to back for 1 s (233 809 frames), every tick
      interval stays 24 001 or 24 002 (±24 allowed).
    - **A whole frame: 6.3 µs of the core in fwtest**, where a transfer
      finishes at once; on the chip at least 60.8 ms of transfer (the
      datasheet's 66 ns a bit), with the core free.
    - **Steady state 65.415 instructions a period, +2.2%** on M1.
      Startup 1 036 288. Code 4 180, static RAM 115 340, stack 188 bytes.
  - **Spec request** (#36): SR-3, the panel's wiring, SPI1's set-up,
    offset, orientation and inversion on the chip (Q-6), the longest
    transfer, and source 16 in fwtest. M2 doesn't depend on it.
  - **Next: M3, keys, encoders, the pot and LEDs.**

### M1 to M9 (firmware side)
- **M1** boot: clocks, interrupts, timer (done; above).
- **M2** screen (done; above).
- **M3** keys, encoders, pot, LEDs.
- **M4** audio.
- **M5** the FM engine.
- **M6** MIDI in.
- **M7** flash storage.
- **M8** UI and original presets (no Yamaha factory voices).
- **M9** packaging, and a raw-image boot path in the app.

### Level 2: real hardware
- **M10** recovery kit.
- **M11** USB-MIDI and the update handler.
- **M12** hardware checklist.

  (SDK as base code, `vendor/` excluded, an unrelated permissive embedded C
  project scored as a control), and publishes scores and file names only.

    Exact captures while waiting would change capture times, and with them

**What:** fixes the similarity audit's self-test, which has failed since M2 with "8 of our 9 files found". The file it missed is `src/font.c`: one constant table whose rows are macro calls on string literals, which JPlag makes 5 tokens of and drops as `TOO_SMALL`. Not a bug in the tool, so:
